answer: Per-identity pigment challenge. Each agent gets a random pigment pattern embedded in a private rendering task; registration requires submitting a measurement that only holds for that pattern. The result is checked against a hidden ground truth, and any duplicate answer creates a detectable ripple across the ledger. Because the challenge is freshly generated per applicant, copying a prior answer fails immediately. Attacker cost: one fresh measurement per identity plus compute to reproduce each pigment, so mass registration scales linearly and the wharf of cheap batch signups collapses.
